* If the event is reported to Bolt directly by the passenger/driver, local ops get notified automatically (see for what events local ops would be notified [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4052680709/High-Risk+Events+Management]). 
* If we become aware of the event only through a police request (passenger/driver did not contact Bolt) then it’s a bit different:
** the case can be escalated directly to the CS Safety team (see _Request Includes a Bolt User as a Suspect_ [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4040950288/Requests+from+Authorities+or+Police])
** CS Safety would open a new tool based on the type of event reported (check *Instruction for the International CS Safety team* [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4040950288/Requests+from+Authorities+or+Police]) that would get escalated to local ops if severe (see link in the first bullet point). 

Hope it’s clear. Let me know if you have questions about it. 

Thank you 

Alessandro

Both can be seen in FROM statements, the bellow one is from the low performing query:

Looking at the [SQL code|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MAPS-1331?focusedCommentId=1266708] behind {{layer_waterway}} UDF, having zoom level 14 the code, the inner zooms table will have only values from {{waterway_z14}} as only this view matches the zoom_level condition, these way the code is simplified to:

{noformat}CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.layer_waterway(bbox geometry, zoom_level integer)
 RETURNS TABLE(geometry geometry, class text, name text, name_en text, name_de text, brunnel text, intermittent integer, tags hstore)
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE PARALLEL SAFE
AS $function$
SELECT geometry,
       class,
       NULLIF(name, '') AS name,
       COALESCE(NULLIF(name_en, ''), name) AS name_en,
       COALESCE(NULLIF(name_de, ''), name, name_en) AS name_de,
       waterway_brunnel(is_bridge, is_tunnel) AS brunnel,
       is_intermittent::int AS intermittent,
       tags
FROM (
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z14
     ) AS zoom_levels
WHERE geometry && bbox;
$function${noformat}

There is nothing complicated in this SQL, it uses geometry in {{WHERE}} field which is has an index. Additionally to this running {{explain}} on top of just this UDF does not indicate any issues:

Currently {{RateLimiter}} uses Redis for attempts synchronization and supports 2 modes:

# {{1 request per X seconds}} - uses Redis’s command SET if not exists with time complexity O(1)
# {{X requests per 1 second}} - uses Redis’s command INCR with time complexity O(1). This approach imply the use of tumbling window with size of 1 second:
!Screenshot 2022-12-22 at 12.57.09-20221222-115715.png|width=1115,height=296!
As for me it is perfect trade of between performance and granularity. But it would be controversial decision if we increased the window size.

So we need alternative solution for the {{X requests per Y seconds}} problem. In my opinion best trade of might be a hopping window with configurable step:

!Screenshot 2022-12-22 at 12.57.00-20221222-115706.png|width=1116,height=376!

From Redis’s point of view the commands sequence will look like:

{noformat}ZREMRANGEBYLEX path_user 0 ($now / 1000 - $hoppingWindowSeconds)
ZRANGE path_user 0 -1 WITHSCORES
ZINCRBY path_user 1 $now / 1000
EXPIRE path_user ($hoppingWindowSeconds + 15){noformat}

Where 1000 is 1 second step, can be configured bigger for performance improving.

Lets count complexity:

# O(log(N)+M) with N being the number of elements in the sorted set and M the number of elements removed by the operation.
# O(log(N)+M) with N being the number of elements in the sorted set and M the number of elements returned.
# O(log(N)) where N is the number of elements in the sorted set.
# O(1)

Since max number of elements in Sorted set is {{hoppingWindowSeconds/step}} we can consider it as constant. Of course performance will be much worse than for tumbling window but time complexity is still O(1).

At the end I’d like to add that  it may make sense for some use cases to allow increasing size of tumbling window. For example 5 second windows with O(1) time complexity may serve needs in some circumstances better than hopping window.

PS. Of course we can add sliding window, but as for me the performance price is too high and the hopping window serves our needs.

Need to build app without dynamic modules, so that they are downloaded during app usage.

"W{color:#333333} _hy the eater needs the invoice with their details visible_" -> Not their, but with edited details (to their requested company details): to many companies in Lithuania if you want a refund (e.g. for a company TB and you spent your money first), you need to have an invoice with the companies details (not personal details (they are not valid for the refund)) and Bolt provides only receipts/invoices with personal information.{color} 
So, although it is inconvenient, eaters go to provider shops and get the invoices with changed details (but only for the food order); for the delivery, they have to request it from the courier (since he is working with a "legal entity" and he is the one delivering, but couriers do not want to waste their time to reach the person and change the details in the document or they have no idea how to do it and they do not bother to learn, unfortunately.
"_how many of these requests do you receive?_" From ±2 to 5 tickets out of 100 come in about this invoice details changing issue (and the biggest issue part is with the couriers for the invoice for delivery). Maybe 5% is not that much in general, but it is a huge issue for business [+|] the same ticket is being solved for a week (since the eater complains that the courier is not willing to do anything, we contact the courier, the courier says ok, and does nothing. Then the eater keeps coming back, and there is nothing we can do..)

I understand that this might be like some kind of forgery, since the courier is the one delivering, not BOLT, and we would edit the document. we had a sync with [~accountid:5d288e648b90870c0e82c093] on this: it turns out that the data is already persisted in {{batch}} and {{batch_order}} tables including info on potential batches which did not happen.

Such that, there is:

*  a row in {{batch}} table per each batch considered (both succeeded and dissolved due to courier rejections). Includes {{courier_id}} field;
* a row in {{batch_order}} table per each order that was proposed in a batch with {{id}} = {{batch_order.batch_id}}. Contains {{is_active: 1 | 0}} that can be used to deduct if was rejected by courier ({{is_active = 0}}) or not.

For example, considering the following scenario: courier accepts the first order, rejects the second proposed in the batch (which ends up delivered as a single order), then accepts the 3rd one in the batch, there will be:

* one row in {{batch}} table
* two rows in {{batch_order}} table
** one for the first order with {{is_active: 1}}
** one for the second with {{is_active: 0}}

Based on the above, we might define “batching effectiveness” (0 to 1) metric as {{# records in batch having (count of batch_order having is_active = 1 > 0)}} divided by {{total # of records in batch}}.

I remember Florian mentioned that those tables are replicated to Presto.

Please let me know if that’s enough and let’s have a sync on this if needed.

A little bit Redis benchmarks (run on my laptop {{redis-benchmark -q -n 100000}}):
O(1) operations have closely-grouped performance:

{noformat}SET: 150602.42 requests per second
GET: 149700.61 requests per second
INCR: 151057.41 requests per second
LPUSH: 152439.02 requests per second
RPUSH: 151285.92 requests per second
LPOP: 155521.00 requests per second
RPOP: 154798.75 requests per second
SADD: 154320.98 requests per second
HSET: 156006.25 requests per second
SPOP: 151515.14 requests per second{noformat}

Sorted Set operations with limited number of entries work with the same performance, therefore I will use ootb tests for a SET and a GET commands:

{noformat}redis-benchmark -n 100000 -q script load "redis.call('zincrby','myzset',1,'two')"
script load redis.call('zincrby','myzset',1,'two'): 153609.83 requests per second{noformat}

{noformat}redis-benchmark -n 100000 -q script load "redis.call('zrange','myzset',0,-1)"
script load redis.call('zrange','myzset',0,-1): 150829.56 requests per second{noformat}

In case we pipeline commands by 2, the total number of executed commands increases in 2 times:

{noformat}redis-benchmark -n 1000000  -P 2 -q          
SET: 296472.00 requests per second
GET: 302663.44 requests per second{noformat}

In case we pipeline commands by 4, the total number of executed commands increases in 3.8 times, so number of processed requests falls for 5 percent:

{noformat}redis-benchmark -n 1000000 -t set,get -P 4 -q
SET: 567215.00 requests per second
GET: 585480.12 requests per second{noformat}


Conclusion:
Of course I can not simulate real life load on my laptop but I don’t expect that Redis performance will fall more than 10 percents for Hopping window comparing to Tumbling window. The network bandwidth must have more affect than pipelining additional 2 commands.
For Hopping window we need to fetch from Redis all steps load (step to count pairs). Therefore it looks like we will have to transfer more data from Redis to services and this may affect performance.

Next steps:

* Add duration monitoring to Rate Limiter
* Implement Hopping window and increased Tumbling window modes
* Make experiments with hopping window performance

Hey [~accountid:5e7dbc872e3fce0c33e8536f], we received the analysis of the external advisor and the main conclusion is the following - the recommendations that the Migration Service makes to Bolt to comply with the relevant laws without citing any proof of Bolt’s being subject to such laws and to engage in clarifications are illegal. We could respond directly to the State Migration Service (not the Directorate of Migration Control from which we received the letter) complaining of and challenging the recommendations.

The main issues with this letter are the following:

# The Migration Service does not have the authority to make exact recommendations to a business. This is more so considering that the recommendation to Bolt to comply with laws is not based on any facts proving that Bolt employs expatriates. The Service has no authority to request that businesses ‘engage with the Service in clarifications’.
# Bolt is not the employer of such couriers/drivers but provides platform access to them, and engaging in business (which the expatriates’ possession of tax identification numbers suggests) does not require the work permit for foreign nationals.
# The letter was issued by the Directorate of Migration Control and signed by its acting head. No regulations of the Directorate are publicly available. Assuming there are no such regulations, the Directorate has no authority to issue the letter for itself or the Migration Service (as, under the regulations of the Service, it is represented by its chief).
# Exceeding by an executive of own authorities is criminally prosecuted if inflicting substantial damage to the rights and interests of entities protected by law. Bolt could complain about the letter to a prosecutor’s office. Before that, however, Bolt could object the recommendations and complain to the State Migration Service (not the Directorate of Migration Control).

Therefore, from the legal point of view 1) it is likely that the Directorate exceeded its authority in sending us this letter, 2) the demands that we received are not applicable to us as we are not the employer of the couriers/drivers.

However, before responding to the Service or taking any actions, please coordinate with [~accountid:5e843e65870bed0c17c06a1f] as to what is best from the public policy point of view.

Hi all,

*TL;DR*

Possible response to the customer could be the following:

_The invoice you receive for Bolt Business aggregates also all the invoices for the Bolt Services used. This is for your convenience while ensuring that all the applicable taxes are calculated and paid according to the relevant laws at all times._ 

_As you as a business customer take up payment for the Bolt Services used by your users we also enable you the access to the relevant driver and the trip data. So that you could validate whether your funds have been used accurately._ 



*In a few more words,*

This all thing touches upon a wider issue, namely what “resale” billing model is actually all about. We deem “resale” merely a billing technicality - _invoice aggregation_ - so that the business customer could receive one payment document as a valid invoice in a way that all taxes are calculated and paid. The transportation service itself is nevertheless provided by a respectively licensed fleet/driver. So the term “resale” should be understood merely in the context of VAT regulations in all the platform-model markets (meaning currently in all other than UK).

Nevertheless the current *request from the business customer is to remove the following data from the monthly informational statement:*

* *driver name and surname*
* *destination address.*

❗ Firstly, we can’t remove this data from the tech end. Moreover, even if we somehow managed to remove this info from the statement it would still be displayed in the Portal (see attached).

!Screenshot 2022-12-27 at 11.14.44 (1).png|width=1778,height=512!

Hence for now I think the above draft-response is the best we can do.



(?) However [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3] perhaps going forward we could/should reassess whether all the data points we share with the business customers are justified. Because:

* non-VAT related legal obligations we fulfill already via the info we provide in the app, in the relevant T&C’s, *and* by sharing the trip summary document with the end user (regardless of the Business billing model). _Which also makes sense because it’s the end user who remains in the contractual relationship with the transportation service provider in each case._
* VAT related information provision obligations we deem fulfilled via invoices we issue to the business customer (single invoice or multiple invoices depending on the Business billing model).

So the data we share with the business customer in the Portal or via any statements should not be about meeting any statutory requirements as such. That ofc shouldn’t mean that sharing the data at hand is automatically not ok - especially if a compliant business customers actually should need this🙂 (e.g. ref to fringe benefits). *But while we seem to be a bit patronizing, should we perhaps further foster the way we facilitate such data sharing? Please advise*🙏 

Happy to jump to a group call on this if needed. To iron out any remaining matters.

Happy holidays!

A.

{{invoicing_refund}} has internal conversion which converts HRK requests to EUR internally, so all places that rely on (amount, currency) from {{invoicing_refund}} are safe.

Overview:

* invoicing_user reacts to {{invoicing_refund}} and uses data from {{invoicing_refund}} event only (/) 
* invoicing-import fetches data from invoicing_refund and compares currency against default company (=country) currency; as long as system country’s currency is updated, we’re good; otherwise refunds will be created with status {{wrong_currency}} and can be retried after system data has been updated (/) 
* ride-haling-billing creates records based on its records, so it must be adjusted to use currency from invoicing_refund 🔛

[~accountid:5d428c9176cb3e0d9d3200df] This issue was in Chat since the early days. The incoming MQTT topic may contain messages that belong to a non-chat domain events, so when this happens and parser detects a foreign event (in this case the event belongs to {{customer_support}}) the chat just ignores it. The log message of course can have a lower severity to prevent polluting crashlytics, but overall there is nothing bad in it. The new chat implementation (aka Cha SDK) ignores foreign MQTT events silently and we’ve just rolled it out globally 100% for {{CA.56.0}} a week ago, so polluting crashlytics shouldn't be an issue anymore. From the stacktrace attached I can see that on the device where this issue was detected {{Chat SDK Tier 0}} feature flag was off, but it won’t be logged when the feature is ON (on the build released recently).
[~accountid:5d43ea3f1a6bf10be6db0f6e] Please update the status here as well. Also, doesn’t this task fit into launches and updates better?

For the reference: here is the [Jira ticket|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CM-3521] where we fixed the similar issue for the new implementation (when {{Chat SDK Tier 0}} feature flag is ON). And here is the [integration Jira ticket|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-17878] in the CLIENTAPP project where this fix was released.

For future reference, based on the discussions with SEWA and our internal discussions:

The possible scenarios were:

# keeping reporting 0 and pay fine in case of detection (up to EUR250k) - risk of detection is rather medium, but SEWA unwilling to recycle our batteries if we are not compliant; also SEWA itself can make a complain to the local municipality and ask for Bolt audit
# starting being compliant: reporting and paying fees to SEWA, question was which entity:
## Bolt SK - as a support for scooters operation in SK - then we need sign some doc between SK and Ops covering this
## Bolt Ops - as an importer - then we need to register and sign new contract with Sewa

We can split payments for several quarter to report the whole fleet for all years of operations. Plus SEWA will not check any CMR or invoices about import, we just need to fill the form. It can be checked by the municipality one day that reported numbers to SEWA are the same with invoicing.

Decision: Scenario 2a - Bolt Operations is an importer and an owner of all e-vehicles and batteries, IG agreement does not give any rights to e-vehicles fo Bolt SK. So in this case contract should be between SEWA and Bolt Operations.

Modified query 

{code:sql}WITH
            count_of_orders AS (
SELECT
	ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_orders,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
WHERE
etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.state='finished'
GROUP BY
	1
            ),
            count_of_fraud_orders AS (
SELECT
	ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_inapp_fraud_orders,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.payment_method_group = 'cash' THEN etl.order_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_cash_fraud_orders
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
	WHERE
		etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
			AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
			AND ot.state = 'finished'
			AND ot.price_review_status = 'ok'
			AND ot.price <> ot.ride_price
			AND co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                    AND (
(etl.user_price_eur <= 1 AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 500 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 60))
OR  
(etl.country_code = 'ng' AND DATEDIFF(day, uu.created, etl.created)<= 7 AND (oc.pickup_distance <= 100 OR oc.pickup_duration <= 30) AND ROUND(etl.rider_discount*1.00/etl.partner_price,2) >= 0.45)
)  
		GROUP BY
			1
            )
            SELECT
	etl.city_id || ':' || etl.order_id AS KEY,
	1 AS fraud_campaign_code_cash_out
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON co.id = etl.order_id AND co.city_id = etl.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try as ot ON ot.city_id=etl.city_id AND etl.order_id=ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.fraud_order_check  AS oc ON oc.order_id = etl.order_id AND oc.city_id = etl.city_id
LEFT JOIN count_of_orders AS x ON x.driver_id = ot.driver_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu ON uu.id = etl.user_id
LEFT JOIN count_of_fraud_orders AS y ON y.driver_id = ot.driver_id
WHERE
	etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
	AND co.campaign_code IS NOT NULL
	AND co.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)

The response of the external counsel:

_From a preliminary view of the below, there may be some alignment that needs to be done in connection to the Bolt Food terms and the B4B model._

_In accordance with the Bolt Food T&Cs (Art. 7.1), the restaurant undertakes to issue a valid cash register receipt which is delivered to the end-user. This is a B2C operation, mandatory in accordance with Romanian law for any retail business which accepts cash or card payment from the general public (receipts issued by cash registers are traceable in real-time by the fiscal authorities, while cash transactions or bank account transfers are not, therefore it is mandatory for businesses such as restaurants to issue receipts for all payments received)._

_This would apparently not fit the B4B scenario, where the buyer of the food is the Business Customer/Bolt, depending on the invoicing model. There is a lesser risk where the buyer is the Business Customer, because this would be similar to a business expenses account of the employee - noting, however, that it would be necessary for the employee to keep the receipts related to the expenses and hand them over to their employer. However, if Bolt would be the customer, there is no direct link between the end-user and Bolt._
_In case of ride-hailing, this is solved by the fact that the driver does not issue any fiscal receipt, everything is handled via platform, by Bolt, on behalf of the drivers.The possible solution would be to amend the Bolt Food T&Cs and for the restaurants to accept the interpretation that, in the case of Bolt Business, they are not under an obligation to use the cash register, because they are not directly receiving payment from the buyer via cash or card. This would mean that they would have to implement a new billing option, i.e. invoicing the Business Customer/Bolt for each transaction, while the end-customer would not be receiving any fiscal receipt, but only a pro-forma document._

_On a separate topic, as regards the difference between the intermediate and aggregation models, for aggregation, Bolt would be deemed as a reseller for VAT purposes and under the obligation to apply VAT to the aggregate invoice (i.e. not only to its own B4B service fee)._

# The file is then sent to the user via an in-app message.
# After the user has downloaded the zip file, they can extract the JSON file and open the JSON file with different applications that can read such a file. For example, Mac users can use the TextEdit app, Microsoft users can open it with Notepad. The file can also be viewed with a web browser, either with Google Chrome or Mozilla. If the user does not have a default app for opening a JSON file, then the system falls back to one of the default browsers that the user has downloaded on their device. Hence, it can look like the file is coming somewhere from the internet. Although, when the user would check the URL of the file, then they can see that the file does not come from a website, but from their device (check the screenshot).

Phillip’s answer on the issue (12m ago): 

”Motor third party liability, or a variant thereof, is a statutory cover in almost all of Bolt’s operating jurisdictions. The insurance covers the owner or driver of a vehicle for his liabilities to any third parties, including passengers, for bodily injury or property damage that may result from his actions or in-actions whilst the vehicle is in use.This line of insurance is very highly regulated in most jurisdictions, with strict control of the policy wordings, limits, and insurable interest. In many jurisdictions specific extensions of cover are required to operate a vehicle for hire and reward, in the absence of said extensions the insurance is deemed invalid and the driver uninsured. *Note: Injured third parties will typically not be affected by such exclusions and have the benefit of coverage, or access to either government or industry-run “uninsured driver pools”.*_Current StatusAs a platform operator, and with no contractual or financial interest in the vehicles or drivers who operate on our platform, Bolt is not in a position to take up insurance to address the statutory motor third-party liabilities that are legally required to operate a motor vehicle in most jurisdictions. As noted above, in most jurisdictions particularly in Europe, the only party that may take up these insurances are the named owner, or named driver of the vehicle. In this respect Bolt is reliant upon each and every driver to present valid documentation demonstrating the existence of a legally binding contract of insurance for operation of a vehicle, and where required, specific endorsement showing cover for commercial hire and reward.Bolt’s operates a comprehensive process for collation and validation of documentation in all jurisdictions, and wherever possible validates the status of these documents against publicly available registers of insurance. Documents are checked for authenticity, validity and any evidence of tampering, with periodic auditing and requests for document updating taking place at least bi-annually.Whilst Bolt is reviewing options for contingent motor insurance under general liability and non-owned auto insurances, it should be understood that these coverages can only operate on a contingent basis, i.e. that the principal liability remains with the driver or vehicle owner. Moreover, Bolt can only purchase such insurances with defined limits of cover as these are not subject to the same provisions, and reinsurance pools, as statutory motor third party covers.”_

Phillip also said that the General Liability and Cyber *were in progress (12 months ago)*, thus I would have expected that they got completed by now (?). Difference might be that we were discussing EU markets not UA, which is fully localised business.

{{Subquery Scan on "*SELECT* 10" (actual execution time ~9ms)}}and {{Subquery Scan on "*SELECT* 11" (actual execution time ~9ms)}}both of them looks that were not executed, the time spent looks to be associated with the 2 workers which were launched.

{{SELECT * 10}} stands for below part which should never be executed (and indeed it is not but the Seq scan preparation takes a lot of time):

{noformat}-- etldoc: waterway_z12 ->  layer_waterway:z12
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z12
         WHERE 14 = 12{noformat}

{{SELECT * 11}} has same issue as {{SELECT * 10}}:

{noformat}-- etldoc: waterway_z13 ->  layer_waterway:z13
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z13
         WHERE 14 = 13{noformat}

Removing the 2 selects from the original query decreases the query runtime from ~20ml → 0,2 ms. Both these selects have a where condition for waterway which has an index but still SQL tries to use Seq scan.

One interesting fact that if we try to use the zoom=13, this specific query will use Index scan and will execute instantly.

{noformat}-- etldoc: waterway_z13 ->  layer_waterway:z13
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z13
         WHERE 13 = 13{noformat}

*There are two approaches to fix the issue:*

# Optimise the SQL query by removing SQL queries which will never be executed, for exempla the {{SELECT * FROM waterway_z12 WHERE 14 = 12}}
# Disable completely the Seq scan, tried setting `*SET* enable_seqscan = *OFF*;` before execution of the query and got instant result.

*Network refactoring testing summary:*

Below mentioned setup network variations were covered, listed by priority and most likely use-case on field:

* Wi-Fi access point, connected to internet with ethernet cable
* Direct cellular from test device using SIM (+ falling back to Wi-Fi and vice-versa)
* Mobile hotspot with SIM, device connected to hotspot via Wi-Fi
* Mobile hotspot with SIM, device connected to hotspot via Wi-Fi, proxied through Mac

Tested on:

PA.2.02 (1330723), Lenovo TB-X505L (10.0); Sunmi V2 Pro (7.1.2) and PP.2.02 (1330724.473504349), iPad 6th gen (15.4)



Clearly visible improvements:

* In general it feels like network notifications for user are more clear and behaviour in hectic conditions is overall more reliable.
* Not once I didn’t see problem of occasional “No internet connection” snack-bar after internet re-establishment - looks fixed ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPX-820|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPX-820|smart-link];[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPX-385|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DPX-385|smart-link]).
* Re-establishing connection quicker when access point recovers internet connection.

Improvement ideas:

* On average it takes 25-30s to display “Bolt Food service is temporarily unavailable”, would it make sense to make it come up bit earlier? Need to be careful here to not start spamming user.
* “Bolt Food service is temporarily unavailable” notification - maybe we should revisit this message as it might be misleading that our service is down (or is it wrong impression to me only?), although could be network provider issue for example.

Other

* Saw slow recovery when switching between cellular signal generations (4G <-> 3G) but only while connected through Mac proxy - not realistic case in reality.

After some research it was figured out that the issue has multiple layers:

* Android 5.1 and below does not have TLSv1.2 enabled by default. So all SSL [requests are handled via TLSv.1|https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/net/ssl/SSLEngine.html#default-configuration-for-different-android-versions]. According to the referenced documentation TLSv1.2 is enabled by default starting with Android 5.0 (API 20+), but it’s not exactly true as the issue is reproducible on all androids below the version 6.0, so probably 5.0 was some transition version where they wanted to enable it by default, but something went wrong.
* This issue affects not only establishing MQTT connection, but all HTTPS requests in the app in general. The reason why HTTPS requests to the Bolt endpoints work is that client apps (Rider and Driver) patch HTTP client to use TLSv1.2 forcibly (here is [the patch|https://github.com/bolteu/android-app-client/blob/develop/network/src/main/java/eu/bolt/client/network/di/module/ForceTls12PreLolipopUtil.java] in Rider and here is [the similar patch|https://github.com/bolteu/android-app-driver/blob/develop/app/src/main/java/ee/mtakso/driver/utils/TlsV12SocketFactory.kt] in Driver). 
* Bolt Chat uses MQTT client implementation from [Hive MQ|https://github.com/hivemq/hivemq-mqtt-client/] and in their repository a [similar issue|https://github.com/hivemq/hivemq-mqtt-client/issues/511]. From the comments of the main contributor in this issue it becomes clear that MQTT client doesn’t use {{SocketFactory}} to patch it in the same way as HTTP client is patched by the client apps. However in the very same issue there are suggested a few workarounds:
** One is to use Google Play Services utility which actually also [the official recommendation|https://developer.android.com/training/articles/security-gms-provider] from Google: to update security providers in the apps running on Android 5 and below manually using this Play Services utility. Tests show that after calling {{ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded(context)}} MQTT client start working just fine. The problem is not all Android devices has Google Play Services on board (eg. Huawei). We do support HMS powered devices that may not Play Services on board, but HMS was officially launched in Dec 2019 while Android 6 (that doesn’t have TLS problem anymore) was released in Oct 2015. So in theory this fix should cover the majority of the supported devices.
** Another is to use [Conscrypt|https://github.com/google/conscrypt] library from Google which [Android 11+ relies on|https://developer.android.com/training/articles/security-ssl#ssl-sockets-use-conscrypt-ssl-engine-by-default] by default. Adding this dependency and calling {{Security.insertProviderAt(Conscrypt.newProvider(), 1)}} as recommended in the comments help establishing MQTT connection as well. The problem with this solution is that Conscrypt library is quite heavy (it adds about 3MB to the app) while Google Play Services are pre-installed in Android and do not affect our applications size. This fix however is universal and can be used on both Google Play, Huawei Mobile Services or any other mobile manufacturer that we may not know.
* There is another potential fix to this issue revealed from the [comment|https://github.com/hivemq/hivemq-mqtt-client/issues/511#issuecomment-972971130] to the issue mentioned above: if the server start supporting TLS below version 1.2 old android devices will be able to connect to the broker without any client changes. The downside of this fix is a weaker security in the communication between clients and the server which potentially could affect not only MQTT connections, but also HTTPs (I’m not a backend engineer, so this is just a hypothesis). In any case downgrading security protocol for older devices is a highly undesirable solution that brings more risks than benefits. 



*Bottom line*: In order to enable chat communication on Android 5.1 and below I would recommend to use one of the following approaches:

# Client apps (Rider, Driver, etc) start using Google Play Services utility on Android 5.1 and below when the application starts to enable the required security protocol for their application. This will allow removing the patches they have at the moment and will fix chat connection at the same time.
# We start using Google Play Services utility internally when we initialise Chat SDK on Android 5.1 and below. We release a new build of Chat SDK and upgrade it in the client apps ourselves. This will fix only Chat connection (HTTP should continue to work using the existing patches), but its implementation is completely on our end.
# We turn off Chat contact option for Android 5.1 and below as probably the number of clients using these old android versions is insignificant. For the reference: Rider’s min supported version is Android 5.0, Driver’s min supported version is Android 4.4. This solution will also affect users with higher Android versions as if at least one participant uses Android 5.1 and below the Chat contact option must be turned off.

Hey [~accountid:60fbd5e28b1a9b006f13d407],

the agreement can be terminated but not without consequences. Even if nothing is regulated in the contract itself, the law takes its place. Claims for damages due to premature termination are not excluded by law. 

To put it briefly: If one of the providers terminates prematurely, the award would have to be restarted because the city has committed itself to selecting at least two providers. The costs of a renewed and premature award procedure could be imposed on us. This is only an example. At the present time, it is not possible to conclusively assess which damage positions could be incurred by us. Premature termination without a material reason is tantamount to non-performance, which could trigger a damage position.
In addition, the termination due to the reduction of the fleet by 50% does not constitute an extraordinary reason, as it is already known to us and we bear the business risk (profitability). 

Please also be aware that the city areas where scooters are to be provided are mandatory. 

Please also be aware that subsequent price increases such as an unlock fee or a price increase per minute are not allowed without consultation and approval with the city. The introduction or increase of such fees and prices are generally not permitted without good cause.

In-app messages are actually the best way to confirm we’re talking to the account owner. Yes, it’s not 100% bullet-proof, but from all the channels we have (in-app, email, phone call) it’s the most secure one. 

We can also trust verified emails (or, if the user contacts us via the email connected to their account, there’s also a possibility to verify their email, more info [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/8671806622098]). 

If the user already sends us an in-app message, there’s no need to ask them to send an email (it’s not safer than in-app messages + it would require the agent to check whether the email is verified and if it’s not, ask the user to verify it). This makes the whole process longer both for our CS and the user. 

So what we can do is to add this to the process (marked with red):

*Step 1: Reply to the reporter*

* Identify the user
* {color:#bf2600}*Ask the user to specify the following:*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*The date of the accident*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*Who was driving the vehicle*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*Vehicle license plate*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*How the accident happened*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*Who is guilty of the accident (+ any additional documents to prove it)*{color}
** {color:#bf2600}*Which parts of the vehicle were damaged*{color}
* Ask if someone is injured
** If someone is injured, but emergency services were not called, advise them to contact emergency services first and contact us again with additional information
*** 🇪🇪 *Estonia:* (6000) 112
*** 🇱🇻 *Latvia:* 112
*** 🇫🇷 *France:* 112
* Ask them if the event has been reported to the police
** If yes, ask for the police reference number or a copy of the police report
** If not, advise them to report this event to the police and forward us the reference number or a copy of the police report, *unless* the accident is minor and there are no injuries or there's no disagreement between the parties involved. 
** *Important:* If there is a disagreement about who is to blame for the accident, the user should always call the police
** In case the accident happened with an object and there is no owner nearby with whom a declaration of accident could be fulfilled, the user must always call the police. If the user will not report the accident to the police, it might be considered a hit-and-run, and the user might be fully charged for vehicle and object repairs.
* Ask the user to fill in the accident report and send us a photo of it
** The accident report papers are in the car's glove compartment or at the nearest gas station
* Ask if they could share a photo or video proof (if they have it)
* If the user does not know where they are located now, provide them with the location from Admin

# add {{aldm.account_id}} to select

{noformat}SELECT
    aldm.date AS date,
    'facebook' AS channel_name,
    CAST(aldm.account_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS account_id,
    CAST(campaign_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS campaign_id,
    CAST(adset_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS adgroup_id,
    CAST(ad_id AS VARCHAR(50)) as ad_id,
    sum(impressions) AS impressions,
    sum(clicks) AS clicks,
    sum(spend) AS cost,
    --sum(spend /  cast(rate as INTEGER)) AS cost,
    CURRENT_DATE AS last_update
FROM
    ng_fivetran_facebook_ads_all.ad_level_daily_metrics AS aldm
    LEFT join  
    
	(
	SELECT id as account_id, lower(max_by(currency , age)) as currency
	FROM ng_fivetran_facebook_ads_all.account_history 
	GROUP BY 1
    ) acc_currency on aldm.account_id = acc_currency.account_id
      
    LEFT JOIN ng_public.currency_exchange_rates cer 
    ON acc_currency.currency = cer.currency 
    AND date_trunc('day', valid_on) = date_trunc('day',date)

WHERE
    aldm.date BETWEEN DATE('2022-12-01') AND DATE('2022-12-01')
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6{noformat}

Can I clarify if you're referring to this part of Hugo’s post?

{quote}*If a user requests it, we perform a refund to their original payment method using the Force Refund button (it is our legal obligation)*{quote}

If so, I think that the message has been misunderstood here. If a rider complains about a higher price due to traffic, you should follow the steps in 🚗  [Rider complains about an overcharge|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360012406780--Rider-complains-about-an-overcharge] for “Traffic problems on a suggested route”, which state: 

{quote}If automation was not applied, *refund the* *_small sum value_* *to the rider’s Bolt Balance*{quote}

So, the process is correct and should be followed as it is. We shouldn’t provide a full refund to a user just because they demand a full refund. We should refund the overpriced amount and only proceed with a full refund to their card if the user later informs us that they’re not happy with the refund being sent to their Balance.

If a rider complains that they are unhappy with a refund to their Bolt Balance (for any reason, not just traffic), we must always provide a refund to their original payment method. As we cannot reverse the Bolt Balance refund, or send partial refunds to a card payment method, we should use the Force full refund option (even though we have already provided a refund to their balance). 

Sorry for the long post, but does this clarify the process for you? I’m working on something else related to refunds this month, so I’ll aim to post another message in the cs-global channel to clarify this for everyone!

Hi Andy!

Thank you for bringing this topic up. 

In general, personal data should be deleted when it is no longer necessary in relation to the purposes for which they were collected or otherwise processed. Data protection regulations do not stipulate the minimum and maximum retention period of recruitment related data, which means that the retention period must be based on statutory retention periods and limitation periods for claims stipulated in applicable country specific law. We do not hold information on all country specific legislation, however the *following retention periods apply in Germany, UK and Estonia:* 

# *Germany.* The retention period for Germany should not exceed six months. A rejected applicant currently has to report discrimination in the application process in writing within two months of the rejection. Pursuant to Section 61b (1) ArbGG in conjunction with Section 15 AGG, a subsequent lawsuit must be filed within three months after the claim has been asserted in writing. Delays (e.g. in deliveries) should be taken into account, which is why *retention time a total of six months seems to be appropriate.*

# *United Kingdom*. The Equality Act 2010 sets out strict time limits for bringing a claim against a current or former employer who has carried out a discriminatory act. This includes omissions on the part of the employer such as making a decision not to provide reasonable adjustment. (section 123(3)(b) Eq Act 2010). While discrimination claims which do not relate to employment must be brought under the Act within six months (minus one day) of the date on which the discriminatory act occurred (section 118(1)(a) Eq Act 2010), the time frame in which an employment discrimination claim must be brought is considerably shorter: proceedings must be brought within three months (minus one day) of the act or acts of discrimination which the claim concerns (section 123(1)(a) Eq Act 2010). *Recommended period is 6 months after notifying candidates of the outcome of the recruitment exercise taking into account the limitation periods of the claims.* 

# *Estonia.* Retention period in Estonia stems from the [+Equal Treatment Act+|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/507032022003/consolide] which states that the limitation period of claim for compensation for damage is one year from the date when the injured party becomes aware or should become aware of the damage caused. *Therefore, the data should be deleted after 1 year of making the recruitment decision.*

The user did try to change destination multiple times, and they were indeed rejected. However this happened because of our fraud rules, as they were deemed suspicious.

Whenever the destination changes, so does the price. This can lead to failed payments and increased CCPO due to overcharges (in this case it can already be seen that the payment failed, it’s likely that the tip was offered to force a failed payment). Drivers should be instructed to only drive riders to the destination that has been successfully logged in the app. 

If you wish to go further and compensate the driver for the estimated price, please consult with your TL and local OPS team before doing so.

h2. Investigation: self-help content

h3. Our content

Currently, we have a self-help article only for AdBlue warning lights: [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4413299442066-AdBlue-is-running-low|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4413299442066-AdBlue-is-running-low|smart-link]

No other warning lights are covered in self-help content. For the rest of them, there’s one relevant article: [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020681759-The-car-has-a-mechanical-issue|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020681759-The-car-has-a-mechanical-issue|smart-link].  It simply tells the user to contact CS if they suspect something is not working in the vehicle or there’s damage.

h3. Competitors' content

* The following competitors have similar articles like [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020681759-The-car-has-a-mechanical-issue|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360020681759-The-car-has-a-mechanical-issue|smart-link] that doesn’t directly address any particular warning lights:
** *Citybee:*  [https://help.citybee.tech/en/articles/4898793-what-to-do-if-the-car-breaks-down|https://help.citybee.tech/en/articles/4898793-what-to-do-if-the-car-breaks-down|smart-link]
** *Carguru:* [What should I do if the car is damaged?|https://carguru.lv/information/faq#title]
** *Fiqsy:* no content
** *Share Now:* [https://www.share-now.com/fr/en/faq/search/?query=damage#how-do-i-report-damages-on-a-car|https://www.share-now.com/fr/en/faq/search/?query=damage#how-do-i-report-damages-on-a-car|smart-link]
** *Free2move:* [What should I do if I notice that the car is damaged when I pick it up?|https://www.free2move-carsharing.com/faq/]

h3. Conclusion

AdBlue is the most straightforward warning light - the yellow one doesn’t really require much attention, as OPS have periodic maintenance checks. The self-help article [https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4413299442066-AdBlue-is-running-low|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4413299442066-AdBlue-is-running-low|smart-link] could be revised because:

* *It's lengthy.* Local OPS maintain AdBlue periodically anyway; therefore the user isn’t required to do anything - so the article shouldn’t be that long.
* *The self-help solution causes friction for the user.*
** The user has to complete a lot of actions:
- the user has to find a gas station where AdBlue is available
- they have to buy it with the fuel card
- they have to top it up
** After all that, the user will likely reach out to CS anyway to request a reimbursement for the time spent or for the AdBlue (if the fuel card was missing or there were problems using it).
** It’s best to inform the user that the yellow warning light is ok and no action should be taken. They won’t be able to drive the car with the red warning light anyway (the car won’t start).

For the rest of the warning lights, it’s best to have the user report and discuss the particular issue with CS so that a precise solution can be provided because:

* most of the warning lights are either critical, or
* the user may not feel safe driving the car anyway.

We need to evaluate what’s the best entry point for other warning light issues. We can’t do it atm though because we have no access to data.

Hi Ioana!

Sadly, I am not able to provide you with the specific thresholds as this is internal information only privy to the fraud team. However, I can say that these thresholds look at things like order velocity and type in a specific timeframe.

To rephrase, please note that this driver being a “false positive” is actually quite suspicious and irregular. The rules are built in a way that the conditions that the driver has to fill are near impossible to happen *in reality*. Him reaching the set-out conditions *is not normal*. However, we took into account that this is a cash-heavy market and a busy time and have given him the benefit of the doubt - hence suggesting compensation.

As of this moment, we do not have reason to consider changing the thresholds as these are already considerate of cash markets based on a single already suspicious case. How your local team can help out is to collecting and then escalating any groups of irregularities. Single cases just do not make up a business case for our analysts to continue. 

We can only suggest you consult the billing team as there is not one person who can help out and each team has its own allocation based on different weeks/days/times of the day dealing with different issues. We do not have an overview of this allocation for another team. 

Wishing you a wonderful new year,

* Transportation services – according to applicable law and limited to:
** carrier’s liability
** air - 19 SDRs per kilogram
** sea - 666.67 SDRs per parcel, or 2 SDRs per kilogram, whichever is greater
** rail - [2 / 8.33 / 17/19] SDRs per kilogram
** land (international) – 8.33 SDRs per kilogram
** land (domestic) – local domestic transportation rules
* Warehousing
** storage – replacement value up to EUR 1MM
** additional services – according to Civil Code (Estonia) up to twice the amount of the service
** damage other than to the goods – EUR 300K in each calendar year
* Customs services
** Fines – only in case of gross negligence or wilful misconduct, up to the amount of the Goods but no more than EUR 300K in each calendar year
* All services - no liability for indirect or consequential losses

Hi both, 

This request has unfortunately not been able to be prioritised due to bigger projects and priorities. We will look at this as soon as possible. 

My initial assessment was that our website would be covered by the Price Indication Directive (EU Directive 98/6/EC) which has been implemented in Sweden through various changes in legislation but primarily in the Price Information Act (Prisinformationslagen (2004:347)). The general rule is that pricing information must be provided in a clear and precise manner and if no exact price can be provided we need to provide information on how the price is determined. The information needs to be accessible for the consumer and this is the information we are providing both in the app and on the website. * Drivers can keep their driver score and acceptance rate above the threshold by balancing between the two

I thought it will be possible to first migrate to supported LTS env on databricks and then to spark 3 but it turned out that it must be done at the same time, because:

* if I bump the runtime only the job fails
* if I release a new version of a job and run it with old runtime it fails as well

The problem is that currently unversioned (latest) jobs jars are used so if I release a new version of the job it will be failing unless I bump the runtime version. This works in the opposite as well, when runtime bump will go first. 

To mitigate this I need to:

* release the versioned jar of the job that is currently used (as well as cluster.jar)
* change latest to versioned in tf scripts
* apply the changes
* release the versioned jar form master branch 
* change the version of the jar and version of the runtime in tf scripts
* apply the changes

{code:sql}
with etl as (
select 
co.order_id,
co.city_id,
co.user_price,
co.country_name,
co.user_price_eur,
co.city_name, 
co.order_category_name, 
uor.decision.pre_auth.amount.value as preauth_value,
co.fraud_label,
c."group"
from ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
left join archive_analytical.user_order_request uor on co.fraud_calculation_id = uor.id 
left join ng_public.company_order_search_filter AS s ON cast(s.id as varchar) = cast(co.order_id as varchar) AND cast(s.city_id as varchar) = cast(co.city_id as varchar)
left join ng_public.admin_search_category c ON s.filter_search_category_id = c.id
where co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) AS date)
and uor.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) AS date)
and uor.decision.pre_auth.amount.value > 0
and co.order_state = 'finished' 
), 
corrections as (
select 
p.order_id,
p.city_id,
p.n,
p.price_component_price,
row_number() over (partition by cast(p.order_id as varchar)||cast(p.city_id as varchar) order by p.n desc) row_nr
from ng_public.etl_pricing_order_price_components p
where p.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) AS date)
and p.price_component_type = 'correction'
),
count_destinations AS (
SELECT b.city_id,
b.order_id,
COUNT(*)-1 as count_of_destinations_changes
FROM ng_public.company_order_destination b
LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city sc ON b.city_id = sc.id
WHERE b.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) AS date)																																								-- COUNTRY FILTER 
GROUP BY 1,2
having COUNT(*)-1 < 1
),
other_fees as (
SELECT a.order_id,
a.city_id, 
a.other_component_final
FROM ng_public.etl_order_price_components a
WHERE a.other_component_final > 0.1
AND COALESCE(a.paid_wait_day_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.paid_wait_night_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.price_review_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.toll_road_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.long_trip_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.min_price_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.surge_component_final,0) = 0
AND COALESCE(a.cancellation_fee_component_final,0) = 0
--AND COALESCE(a.booking_fee_component_final,0) = 0 
AND a.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) AS date)
)
select 
co.country_name,
count(case when preauth_value < 1.000001*user_price and fraud_label = true then preauth_value end) as fraud_orders_count,
count(*) as all_orders_count,
count(case when preauth_value < 1.000001*user_price and fraud_label = true then preauth_value end)*1.000000/count(*) as count_percentile,
sum(case when preauth_value  < 1.000001*user_price and fraud_label = true then user_price_eur end) as fraud_orders_sum,
sum(user_price_eur) as all_orders_sum,
sum(case when preauth_value  < 1.000001*user_price and fraud_label = true then user_price_eur end)/sum(user_price_eur) as sum_percentile
from corrections c 
join etl co
on co.order_id = c.order_id and co.city_id = c.city_id
join count_destinations as cd 
on co.order_id = cd.order_id and co.city_id = cd.city_id
join other_fees o
on co.order_id = o.order_id and co.city_id = o.city_id
where row_nr = 1
group by 1
order by 2 desc{code}

So, here is the summary of what happening: 
We are showing the correct data for both CC and Invoicing companies, but our labels are misleading.

What we show on the “Current Spent” tile is the debit of the company in the current month. It is not what the company spent in the current month.

Take our company as an example (id: 25870): [https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/25870|https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/25870|smart-link]
It is an invoicing company, but we don’t do monthly payments. Therefore we are showing the total amount we owe, not just what we spent in the current month. This amount will just increase.

Take Raido’s company as an example (id: 229709) : [https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/229709|https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/229709|smart-link]
It is a CC company, but due to a bug with the new payment flow, one of the orders with the value of   3+ eur was not charged. Therefore this company, although a CC, has a debit. If this debit gets paid, we will see {{0.00}}, once there is no debit.

Take the reported company (id: 215437): [https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/217727|https://business.prelive.bolt.eu/company/217727|smart-link]
It is also a CC company and all payments worked fine. Therefore we will see {{0.00}} in the “Current Spent” tile.

Last but not least, if we go to the dashboard of a invoicing company, that pays the invoicing every month and has paid for the current month, we will be able to see the amount that is in debit in the current month. 
This is the same as the amount spent in the month, but just because of the model of company in the perfect scenario.
If we want to show the “Amount spent in the month” we can easily do it by summing the value of the rides, regardless if there is any debit in the company or not.

What we can do for this bug is to make better labels, but the business logic for the information we are currently showing is matching.

{code:sql}SELECT 
x.country_name,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id) AS total_count_drivers,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Enrol' THEN x.driver_id END) AS count_enrolled_drivers,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to driver status' THEN x.driver_id END) AS count_not_enrolled_drivers_due_status,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to fraud orders' THEN x.driver_id END) AS count_not_enrolled_drivers_due_fraud,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to both driver status and fraud orders' THEN x.driver_id END) AS count_not_enrolled_drivers_due_status_and_fraud,
ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Enrol' THEN x.driver_id END)*1.00/COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id),2) AS ratio_enrolled,
ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to driver status' THEN x.driver_id END)*1.000/COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id),3) AS ratio_not_enrolled_drivers_due_status,
ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to fraud orders' THEN x.driver_id END)*1.000/COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id),3) AS ratio_not_enrolled_drivers_due_fraud,
ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.enrol_label = 'Not enrol due to both driver status and fraud orders' THEN x.driver_id END)*1.00/COUNT(DISTINCT x.driver_id),2) AS ratio_not_enrolled_drivers_due_status_and_fraud
FROM (
WITH driver_stats AS ( -- count how many orders were marked by our driver fraud profiling jobs from the past 3 months
SELECT
ot.driver_id,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN faoa.action IS NOT NULL THEN ot.order_id END) AS count_fraud_orders_past_three_months
FROM ng_public.company_order_try AS ot
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fraud_action_order_action AS faoa ON faoa.city_id = ot.city_id AND faoa.order_id = ot.order_id
WHERE ot.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND ot.state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1
),
clean_label AS (
SELECT
fd.id AS driver_id,
fd.status AS fleet_driver_status,
fdr.status AS fleet_driver_root_status,
da.action AS fraud_driver_action,
fdsb.reason AS driver_schedule_blocking_reason,
CASE WHEN (fd.status <> 'active' OR fdr.status <> 'active' OR da.action IS NOT NULL OR fdsb.reason IS NOT NULL) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_clean
FROM ng_public.fleet_driver AS fd -- overall driver status
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fraud_action_driver_action AS da ON fd.id = da.driver_id AND CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN da.created AND da.finish_time -- fraud related blockings from profiling jobs
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_driver_scheduled_blocking AS fdsb ON fd.id = fdsb.driver_id AND CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN fdsb."start" AND fdsb."end" -- all other scheduled blocking like documents expire
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_driver_root AS fdr ON fdr.id = fd.driver_root_id -- overall driver block status 
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
),
main_query AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
fd.id AS driver_id,
sc.name AS city_name,
sc2.name AS country_name,
cl.is_clean,
ds.count_fraud_orders_past_three_months,
CASE
	WHEN sc2.code IN ('at', 'es', 'fr', 'gb', 'mt', 'nl', 'pt', 'se', 'de', 'ie', 'it', 'no') AND ds.count_fraud_orders_past_three_months > 3 THEN 0 -- WE 3+
	WHEN sc2.code IN ('az', 'by', 'cy', 'ee', 'ge', 'hr', 'hu', 'kz', 'lt', 'lv', 'pl', 'ro', 'rs', 'sk', 'ua', 'am', 'cz') AND ds.count_fraud_orders_past_three_months > 5 THEN 0 -- CEE 5+
	WHEN sc2.code IN ('gh', 'ke', 'ng', 'tn', 'tz', 'ug', 'za') AND ds.count_fraud_orders_past_three_months > 9 THEN 0 --- AFRICA 9+
	WHEN sc2.code IN ('cl', 'do', 'ec', 'eg', 'iq', 'lb', 'lk', 'mx', 'pe', 'py', 'sa', 'th', 'tv') AND ds.count_fraud_orders_past_three_months > 4 THEN 0 --- OTHERS 4+
ELSE 1 END AS is_below_threshold
FROM ng_public.fleet_driver AS fd LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_company fc ON fd.company_id = fc.id  
LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city AS sc ON sc.id = fc.city_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_country AS sc2 ON sc2.code = sc.country_code
LEFT JOIN driver_stats AS ds ON ds.driver_id = fd.id
LEFT JOIN clean_label AS cl ON cl.driver_id = fd.id
)
SELECT DISTINCT
mq.driver_id,
mq.city_name,
mq.country_name,
CASE
	WHEN mq.is_clean = 1 AND mq.is_below_threshold = 1 THEN 'Enrol'
	WHEN mq.is_clean <> 1 AND mq.is_below_threshold = 1 THEN 'Not enrol due to driver status'
	WHEN mq.is_clean = 1 AND mq.is_below_threshold <> 1 THEN 'Not enrol due to fraud orders'
	WHEN mq.is_clean <> 1 AND mq.is_below_threshold <> 1 THEN 'Not enrol due to both driver status and fraud orders'
END AS enrol_label
FROM main_query AS mq
WHERE mq.country_name IN ('Paraguay')
) AS x 
GROUP BY 1 {code}

* Order is created and getVehicles polling is triggered, which in turn triggers getLocationConfig - cross-domain switcher has information about carsharing order
* Order is cancelled, invalidation key for carsharing order is cleared automatically, which triggers getLocationConfig - it still returns carsharing order even if it is finished (there is a lag between order finish and getting actual information from getLocationConfig)
* User goes to Overview screen, getVehicles polling is triggered, but invalidation keys didn’t change because carsharing key was already cleared earlier

In this case getLocationConfig will not be called until new order is started (or location is changed, or locale is changed)

The recommendation from privacy side is not to implement the feature if no additional safeguards could be put in place.

As for the risks, the primary one is - given the fact that significant part of the exports may require manual verification -  a mistake in this additional process. In case this risk materialises, the impact could be as follows:

* disclosing additional data to 3rd party that wasn’t involved in engaging specific worker, could be deemed a breach of the GDPR. Considering the scope and the context of the breach, Bolt may be required to inform the supervisory authority about the incident.
* in case of confirmed data breach, Bolt could be also exposed to civil claim lodged by the individual, whose data has been unlawfully disclosed.

The risks above could be mitigated by putting control process in place, or - in the future when it will be feasible- producing the exports that include the workers employed by specific 3rd party only.

Now, I see the driver is confused about the report’s calculation logic as well as the balance calculation logic. Please note the report and the payouts follow different logics. The report only reflects what was earned/deducted within a specific month, while payouts can include some rides from previous/next month as we do our payouts for 1 calendar week, and days of 2 different months can happen to be in one week.

About the report;

Yes, driver’s earnings in the report add up to £4451.3, however there is another big category on the lower right corner called “_Other Potential Deductions_” in the amount of £758. That includes Bolt Commission and any other potential fee/deduction. So the logic in the report is {{Fare Breakdown + Other Income Breakdown - Other Potential Deductions}}. So, £4451.3 - £758 = *£3693.3 is the driver’s actual earnings in December* and what the driver’s December payout should have been. 

However, Driver’s total in December was *£4324.6* because he also got paid for the last few days of November (£631.3) as we do our payouts weekly and, last days of November & first days of December coincided. Therefore, *£3693.3 + 631.3 = £4324.6*.

	from 
	(

		cot2.price_currency, cot2.ride_price, cot2.price

		where cot2.driver_id = 287836
		and coalesce(co.payment_method_type, 'default') = 'default'
		and cot2.price_review_finished_timestamp + interval '1' hour >= date('2020-01-01')
		and cot2.price_review_finished_timestamp + interval '1' hour < date('2022-10-01')
	)
	group by 1, 2, 3
),
balance_entry as 
(
	select date(bbd.created + interval '1' hour) as date_id,
	bbd.currency,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'fee' then amount end) as fee,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'app_payment' then amount end) as app_payment,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'payment' then amount end) as payment,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'payout' then amount end) as payout,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'refund' then amount end) as refund,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'compensation' then amount end) as compensation,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'campaign' then amount end) as campaign,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'custom_compensations' then amount end) as custom_compensations,
	sum(case when bbd.transaction_type = 'custom_deductions' then amount end) as custom_deductions
	from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_driver bbd 
	left join ng_public.invoicing_client ic on ic.id = bbd.entity_id
	where bbd.entity_type = 'driver' and ic.external_id = 287836
	and bbd.created + interval '1' hour >= date('2020-01-01')
	and bbd.created + interval '1' hour < date('2022-10-01')
	group by 1, 2
)
select coalesce(be.date_id, ce.date_id) as date_id,

Hi Armin!

If I may offer some help here.

Ride-hailing

Bolt Operations OU is holding the ride-hailing licence, while Bolt Services RO SRL is acting as the local subsidiary that represents Bolt Operations OU in relation to the RO authorities. Some changes may take place due to the legislation, but at the moment we operate according to this system.

E-scooters

Regarding the scooters, Bolt Operations OU manages the rental activity, is the owner of the e-scooters, while Bolt Services RO SRL provides services for Bolt Operations OU: storage of scooters, repairs and maintenance, collection, etc., so it is the entity that concludes local contracts with third parties (rent, invoices, mechanics, etc). Regarding the relationship with the authorities, Bolt Services RO SRL acts as the first point of contact with local stakeholders.

Yes, some local governments insist on issuing the authorisations to the local entity, for the simple reason that they do not understand the attributes of the two entities. Although we explained to them, several times, that Bolt Operations OU is responsible for the services, they claim that they cannot give authorisation to a foreign entity, but only to the entity on the territory of Romania. It is a slight misunderstanding of the European legislation on their part. 

As far as we are concerned, when we apply for authorisation, we make the request on behalf of Bolt Operations OU and explain that Bolt Services RO SRL only has a representative role.

From a legal and tax point of view, it doesn't affect us, or at least that's what our Tax analysis showed. Nothing changes regarding our internal process. We are also covered by the intra-group agreement, in case additional questions may arise.

Thanks,

Sorina

[~accountid:6215e9e897d313006ba50898] the width of the message bubble is adjusted automatically based on the text with it contains. We can not expand the bubble adding some padding to the right in this case without affecting other messages (eg. the regular multiline text like on the screenshot on the left). Lets assume this is not a pick-up note that has an issue, but some random multiline text message that unlike in the example on the left screenshot has the last line a bit longer than it is now:

!Screenshot 2023-01-09 at 09.28.14.png|width=25%!

This is what it will look like. I’ve just photoshopped the text on the screenshot you sent and on the real device there won’t be the overlap, but the space will be the same as on the pick-up note. I suppose can get the idea. So my point is, there is always a case when the last line of the text is too close to the time view and shifting the text to the left doesn’t solve the problem. Besides complex width computations based on text measurements in a list are very performance sensitive, so this will degrade the scrolling animation quality. So I’d suggest to just make the space between the time view and the last message line a little bigger than it is. It would be an easy solution that solves the problem universally without affecting the scrolling performance.

Hey!

Our general approach here is not to set any punitive KPIs - otherwise we have a high reclassification risk (meaning - the drivers would be considered our employees).

Any activity threshold should not be applied (for example: if you do less than X rides, you will be downgraded to “Basic” category OR Activity rate less than 65% results in account suspension).

But this doesn’t mean that we couldn’t apply different approach - bonus for activity (business days, from 07-09 and 16-18, the base fee is higher and commission lowered to 15%), just we cannot apply the KPIs (_like: do 10 rides, get 5 EUR extra. 20 rides - 12 EUR extra. 50 rides - 30 EUR extra_).

//edit: even if we apply “carrot” approach, the drivers are free to decline the orders. I think we have some technical solution for “rush hour” mode, but not sure where it is/was implemented.

[~accountid:5d8ca37816bcf20dd1c67717] Here are my thoughts on each point:

+*Employers' liability (EL):*+

From my understanding, this is not a compulsory insurance for us to have in the Ukraine, unlike the USA, UK and some EU countries. 

I believe the law in the Ukraine states: 

{color:#ff991f}_Employers must provide employees with adequate means of protection against hazards of occupational injury and disease that may occur during work. -_ {color}[{color:#ff991f}_Link to law page_{color}|https://www.hr-inform.co.uk/employment_law/employment-law-in-ukraine]

But I would suggest we check with the local teams or with HR to see what we have in place to meet local laws. 

Therefore, we can then reply to McDonald's saying we do not have EL, but we meet local laws by dong *_{……………}_* 

+*General civil liability (GL):*+

Again from my understanding this is not a compulsory insurance for us to have in the _Ukraine_. 

We could tell McDonald's that we do not have GL; but we are happy to have the contract structured so Bolt is responsible for damages to any of McDonald’s property upto a 5m Dollars.

However, this would require input from other areas of the business due to the potential exposures. 

+*Thoughts on EL & GL Points:*+

My concern for us; is if we tell McDonald's we do not have EL or GL, then they might see us as a _naive_ or _irresponsible_ operation; and therefore, they might not want to do business with us. 

+*Civil liability of owners and users of vehicles*+

As mentioned already, this is not our responsibility to buy, but I would suggest we ask users to send us proof they have insurance like we do in other countries. 

We can reply to McDonald’s saying these are not our vehicles so we do not insure them or have the authority to insure them.

However, we do ask all delivery drivers to supply proof they have insurance. Therefore, we meet this condition. 

+*Cyber Liability (CL)*+

Like EL and GL, this is not a compulsory insurance for us to buy in the _Ukraine_. 

But, we could explain we have very strong and robust cyber security and risk management systems. So as per the GL, we could suggest having the contract structured so Bolt is responsible for this. 

But again this would require input from other areas of the business due to the potential exposures. 

*Final thoughts:*

I am not sure of the relationship we have with McDonald’s, but it might be worth a conversation to explain what we do and also explain that with the current situation in the Ukraine buying insurance there is a challenge. 

I would also suggest that many of their current partners who bought insurance before the war might now not be insured. As many insurance policies have a _War Exclusion Clause._ 

This clause excludes coverage for acts of war, such as invasions, insurrections, revolutions, military coups, and terrorism.

Therefore, I would be surprised if any of their Ukrainian partners have _valid_ insurance. 

 

Hope this helps and let me know if you would like to explore buy GL, GL and/or CL

Yes, outsourcing this process is definitely possible from data protection perspective. In order for this process to be handled in a compliant manner, the provider that is a party to the sale agreement (which acts as a separate data controller in this capacity), should conclude a data processing agreement with this 3rd party vendor that would set out proper standard for secure data sharing.

There is no requirement for Bolt to be party to such arrangements, as this would be outside of processing activities carried our by Bolt as a data controller.

The internal VoIP state machine was never changed from {{AcceptedCall}} to {{OngoingCall}} for the next 20 seconds until the user reported the bug. All further attempts to Accept the call were unsuccessful because of the invalid current call state which was never reached.

The internal state changes to {{OngoingCall}} after Sinch SDK notifies us to {{onCallEstablished()}} callback which never happened for some reason even though we were subscribed for this listener when the incoming call was initialised. 

There are two possible reasons for this:

* Sinch SDK for some reason doesn’t call {{onCallEstablished()}} callback and it’s stuck in the incorrect state infinitely. In this case we must notify Sinch about this issue and wait while the fix is provided.
* {{SinchCallRepository.onSinchCallEstablished()}} function works incorrectly, so it never reaches the line where we change the internal VoIP state to {{OngoingCall}}. There are three early exist points in this function where two of them contain logs and these messages were not found in the attached log file. The early exist point that doesn’t contain logs is logically unreachable because the function exits only if the current call state {{isActiveCall == false}} and according to the logs the last state set is {{AcceptedCall}} which always {{isActiveCall == true}}. 

----

*Follow up:* based on the attached logs Sinch SDK doesn’t notify us that the call is either established or ended or progressing (none of the callbacks from {{InternalCallListener}}) so we’re stuck in the {{Accepted Call}} state and as a result user is not able to accept the call. 

*Solution:* notify Sinch about this issue explaining what happened during the call and providing them call ID so they could investigate this issue on their end.
